title: Jamison 2013 lumbar disc axial compressive stiffness at baseline (1000 ms) impacts

quantity.name: axial compressive stiffness
quantity.definition: tangent stiffness at maximum load, 1000 ms triangular displacement impact; text gives approximate range only

source.authors: Jamison D, Cannella M, Pierce EC, Marcolongo MS
source.sample: 5 lumbar anterior column units (disc + adjacent vertebrae, posterior elements removed), NDRI donors

protocol.summary: Anterior column units potted, preloaded/preconditioned (Instron, see paper), then displacement-controlled triangular axial compression impacts of 0.2, 0.5, 0.8 mm with durations 80, 160, 320, 400, 600, 800 and 1000 ms (baseline), randomised, 3 s between events; k = tangent stiffness at maximum load; dissipated energy from hysteresis; normalised to the 1000 ms baseline of the same disc and displacement.
how_to_simulate: Model a disc with adjacent vertebral bodies (posterior elements removed) under axial displacement control
Apply triangular compression to 0.2, 0.5 or 0.8 mm with total duration 80-1000 ms
Report tangent stiffness at peak load relative to the 1000 ms case; baseline ~500 N/mm (0.2 mm) to ~850 N/mm (0.8 mm)

extraction.check_notes: Values quoted approximately in Results ('ranged from nearly 500 N/mm (0.2 mm) to 850 N/mm (0.8 mm)'). doi not printed.

pass_rule.rule: |model - mean| <= 1 SD (or inside [min, max] when no SD)
